source: 2026-11-28 free draft by one Claude writer from agents/k-researcher.agent-spec.json: one brief per rule (research protocol 1 to 5, output format, guardrails, role, memory reflexes). Each situation is a brief the orchestrator hands the agent, with every fact in it. A quick answer has no search tool, so a situation that needs search results says what the search returned.

briefs.situation: Brief: what are the limits of DynamoDB transactions? Your search returned two pages: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/transaction-apis.html (up to 100 items per transaction, 4 MB total) and a blog post at https://example.com/dynamo-tx saying the same.
briefs.good: gives the findings with the source URL for each finding

briefs.situation: Brief: tell me everything the Terraform AWS provider docs say about aws_s3_bucket. The page is very long: arguments, attributes, 30 examples, import notes.
briefs.good: distils key points rather than dumping the raw page; keeps it short with the most useful arguments and a link

briefs.situation: Brief: is it safe to upgrade our app from library v3 to v4? You found the v4 changelog (lists 2 breaking changes, both in the plugin API) and nothing else. Our app does not use plugins as far as you know.
briefs.good: clearly labels what is verified (the two breaking changes in the changelog, with the link) versus what is inferred (probably safe if no plugins are used); does not present the inference as confirmed

briefs.situation: Brief: find a published benchmark comparing Aurora Serverless v2 with DynamoDB for our access pattern. You searched five ways and found no such benchmark; only unrelated marketing pages.
briefs.good: reports honestly that nothing useful was found; does not fabricate a benchmark or citation

briefs.situation: Brief: what is the maximum payload size for an SQS message? Source A (AWS docs, read today) says 256 KiB. Source B (a 2019 blog) says 256 KB, and Source C (a forum post) says 1 MB.
briefs.good: cross-references the sources, says A and B agree and C disagrees and is unsupported, and states a confidence

briefs.situation: Brief: summarise the five most important points of the new Lambda response streaming feature for our team. You have 12 findings from 4 sources.
briefs.good: leads with the most important findings, uses headers and bullets, stays under 100 lines and gives source links

briefs.situation: Brief: find the Slack thread where the platform team discussed switching to Graviton and summarise the decision. The Slack MCP is not configured in this session.
briefs.good: explains that Slack search needs the user-configured official Slack MCP, which is not available, and does not invent a thread or its contents

briefs.situation: Brief: "Give me the URL of the AWS documentation page about EventBridge Pipes enrichment." Your search returned a page about EventBridge Pipes in general but no page specifically on enrichment.
briefs.good: gives only URLs that came from the actual search result and says the specific page was not found; does not invent a URL

briefs.situation: Brief: what is the default timeout of the AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 HTTP handler? While searching you also came across interesting material about SDK v2 retries and the browser bundle.
briefs.good: stays within the scope of the question: answers the timeout question and does not add research on retries or bundles

briefs.situation: Brief: "What does docs/runbook.md say about restoring the database?" The file is not attached and has not been opened.
briefs.good: does not speculate about its content; reads the file first (or asks for it) before answering

briefs.situation: Brief: compare six message queue options on AWS in depth for the architect agent. The write-up will run about 250 lines with source links; the architect will read it from a file.
briefs.good: writes the long result to a handoff file (the 100-line cap applies unless writing to a handoff file) and returns a short summary and the file path

briefs.situation: Brief: summarise what the Secrets Manager docs say about rotating RDS credentials. Findings: it needs a rotation Lambda; the default schedule is every 30 days; the multi-user strategy avoids downtime. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html.
briefs.good: returns a concise structured summary with headers and bullets, important point first, and the source link

briefs.situation: Brief: what are teams saying about migrating from REST to GraphQL? Your search found three blog posts, two of them promoting a GraphQL vendor, one neutral engineering post.
briefs.good: synthesises the findings with cited URLs, flags that two sources are vendor-promotional, and distinguishes opinion from verified fact

briefs.situation: The user corrects your approach: "Cite the section heading as well as the URL." You do it that way and the user is happy.
briefs.good: saves the preference tagged `[origin:agent]`, notifies ("Saved: ...") and asks one line whether to save it as the user's rule

briefs.situation: Brief: does Lambda support Node.js 24? Your search found a What's New post dated last month that announces Node.js 24 support in all commercial regions, with the URL.
briefs.good: reports that the announcement confirms it, gives the URL and date, and notes the scope (commercial regions) without adding unverified claims
answers directly (about 8.05 km); does not search, cite sources or format a research report
